framing: He Was Socrates is a macOS native app, not a SaaS — and the fastest way to prove that is to draw the SaaS admin dashboard a 2026 evaluator expects and cross out every panel that would normally exist. The empty admin shell is the architecture diagram: no billing, no team, no integrations, no API keys, no webhooks, no audit logs — because the App Sandbox refuses network egress and inference runs locally via MLX. What's left in the main pane is an iframe of the actual product the user would actually use.
target_persona: Kaggle/DeepMind judges (and engineering-skeptical evaluators) who have just scrolled past forty SaaS-shaped LLM demos and instantly recognize the chrome — sidebar, header, stat cards, breadcrumbs — but pause when every familiar admin surface is greyed-out and crossed-through. Secondary: Two-Weeks-Team org members who get the joke immediately because they've maintained Next.js + Postgres + Docker stacks before and recognize the deliberate restraint.
primary_surface: Single-file self-contained HTML rendered as a classic SaaS admin layout — left sidebar (Workspace / Account / Platform groups, with Bust + Wondering Log as the only active items, everything else struck-through with ⊘ glyphs), top header (brand mark + 'Local · v0.1.0 · macOS 26' crown + struck-through 'Upgrade plan' / 'Invite team' pills + a single live 'on-device' status pill), and a main pane containing a banner, four stat cards (TTFT 192 ms, 0 B egress, $0/mo, — incidents), a two-column grid showing a fake browser-frame iframe of the actual macOS bust UI labeled 'What you'd actually use' alongside a refusal list (/billing → 404 local app, /team → 404 single user, etc.) and the Korean SystemPrompt.swift excerpt verbatim. Stack reference: Next.js + Postgres + Docker — the SaaS we did not build, named on the page as the trap we deliberately avoided. OKLCH color space throughout, system-ui font stack, no external resources.
opus_4_7_capability: Opus 4.7's structural-empathy reasoning — the ability to hold two architectures in mind simultaneously (the SaaS the evaluator unconsciously expects, and the macOS native reality) and render the gap between them as visible negative space. Each greyed-out sidebar item required choosing both a believable SaaS panel name (Billing / Team / Integrations / API keys / Webhooks / Audit logs / Usage) AND the one-word reason it doesn't apply (no billing / single user / sandboxed / on-device / no egress / no cloud / $0/mo). Opus 4.7 keeps the SaaS chrome accurate enough to recognize and the strikethroughs accurate enough to teach.
mvp_scope: One single-file HTML mockup, ~480 lines, that renders convincingly as a SaaS admin overview page on first glance and reveals itself as deliberately-empty SaaS-shell on second glance. The 4-day demo: open the file in any browser, no build step, no server, no dependencies — the same posture the actual app takes. If a judge clicks any of the disabled sidebar items, nothing happens, which is exactly the point.
one_liner_pitch: The familiar SaaS dashboard layout with every SaaS panel crossed out — proving He Was Socrates needs no billing, team, integrations, or API keys because it runs on one Mac.
spec_alignment_notes: All idea.spec.json fields populated (_filled_ratio=1.0); followed spec verbatim. target_persona inherits spec.target_persona.primary (Kaggle/DeepMind judges, technical-leaning English readers) plus secondary (Two-Weeks-Team). primary_surface respects 'single-file self-contained, dark theme, OKLCH, system-ui, no external CDN' from spec constraints. Korean limited per spec.language_policy to: bust subtitle ('답을 주지 않는다. 질문을 돌려준다.') + SystemPrompt.swift excerpt verbatim — English elsewhere. All seven differentiators surfaced (abstention via /api/keys=404 and refusal list, NO-CLOUD via 0 B egress stat + crossed-through network entitlement row, PR-Λ via 192 ms TTFT stat + manifest, 4-function dispatch in build manifest, 1-bit halftone in inline SVG bust, Korean tone-lock in callout, macOS 26 in header crown). TTFT cited as 192 ms (not 6 s baseline) per spec anti-pattern #7. Wondering Log marked 'local' (not as-shipped network feature) per spec anti-pattern. The Pragmatist bias ('ship today, 3-year-old stack, Next.js + Postgres + Docker') is expressed by NAMING the SaaS stack we did not build as the foil — the contrast is the argument.
